## p181 A — Warsaw Soldiers Council asks about Mackensens advance

**Edition context:** The Warsaw query and its later quotation — p181 A / p214 B.

**Related source pages:** [p214 B](214.md#source-p214-b).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-warsaw-the-warsaw-query-and-its-later-quotation--p181-a--p214-b"></a>



**Status:** A 92-character query on p181 is quoted inside a later message on
p214 under a different key. The two direct readings agree at **85 of 92**
aligned positions; their complementary evidence supports a complete query
with every proposed source change recorded. **Source comparison and edition:**
icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro. This is a supplementary message, not a new
solution to an open challenge.

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-warsaw-reading"></a>

### Reading

**Readable German:**

> Erbitten umgehend Nachricht, ob Geruecht vom Anmarsch Mackensens auf
> Warschau wahr. Soldatenrat Warschau.

**Meaning:** The Warsaw Soldiers' Council asks for an immediate report on
whether the rumor of Mackensen's advance on Warsaw is true. The query does
not itself establish that such an advance occurred.

The later message includes the query in its forwarding body:

**Readable German — earlier cross-key repairs, with one additional separator fill:**

> An OKM. Hier einging folgender Funkspruch: Erbitten umgehend Nachricht, ob Geruecht vom Anmarsch Mackensens auf Warschau wahr. Soldatenrat Warschau.

The address and introductory sentence are directly decoded. The display
treats the erased character after `FUNKSPRUCHX` as a second separator,
filling source **3** with **A** to make **AX=X**. This adds one mask fill
to the earlier cross-key edition and completes the 130-position introduction
and quotation. The whole source now has **145/146** fixed labels, at **three
observed substitutions and four mask fills**. The remaining erasure is in
the closing reference.

The boundary fill is editorial: the source permits `1GJKWX`, so X is not
cipher-forced. [Exact fill, quotation mapping and retained footer domain](../experiments/open_targets_continuation/p214_completion_certificate.json).

<a id="edition-cases-military-mackensen-warsaw-prior-publication-and-date-discrepancy"></a>

### Prior publication and date discrepancy

Lasry, Niebel, Kopal and Wacker already discuss the Warsaw query in section
6.4 of [*Deciphering ADFGVX messages from the Eastern Front of World War I*](https://www.apprendre-en-ligne.net/crypto/bibliotheque/PDF/adfgvx.pdf),
DOI [10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461](https://doi.org/10.1080/01611194.2016.1169461).
Their narrative assigns it to **13 November**. The inspected p181 page heading
and intercept header both print **12 November**. The source date is retained
here; the discrepancy is not silently resolved.

The present contribution is the cross-key quotation link, direct source
transcription and exact repair accounting. It does not claim first
decipherment of the query or treat the previously published interpretation
as independent cryptographic evidence.

The same prior body credit applies to the quoted query within **p214 B**.
Its forwarding introduction, cross-key source relationship and damaged footer
are assessed separately in this edition.

The unmodified p181 reading is:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ERBITTENUMGEHENDNACHRICHTOBGERUECHTVOMANMARSCHMACKEN?ENSAUFWARSCHAUWAHRXSOLDATENRATWARSCHAUX
```

</details>

Its only unknown plaintext position comes from the printed invalid coordinate
`C` in group `AACDD`. The later quote supplies the missing `S` in
`MACKENSENS`. Filling source index **17** with `G` preserves all **183 valid
coordinates**; the resulting 92-character text re-encrypts exactly. No
unknown square cell is assigned.

The p214 source decodes as:

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
ANOKMXHIEREINGINGFOLGENDERFUNKSPRUCHX?ERBI3TENUM?EHEN?NACHRICHTOBGERUECHT?OMANMARSCHMACKENSENSAUFWARACHAUWAHRXSOLDATENRATWARSCHA8XXAOKYYXRMYAQY?5X
```

</details>

Its 92-position quotation starts at plaintext index **38**. The p181 text
supports three changes to fixed p214 characters and three erasure fills:

| Quote position, zero based | p181 | Direct p214 | Consequence |
| ---: | :---: | :---: | --- |
| 4 | T | 3 | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |
| 10 | G | ? | One p214 erasure fill. |
| 15 | D | ? | One p214 erasure fill. |
| 35 | V | ? | Fill the invalid printed `S` coordinate in p214. |
| 52 | ? | S | Fill the invalid printed `C` coordinate in p181. |
| 62 | S | A | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |
| 90 | U | 8 | One known-coordinate substitution in p214. |

The p214 substitutions are source indices **242: F→V**, **208: X→D** and
**170: X→V**. The fills are **4: –→G**, **56: –→G** and **165: S→V**.
The earlier quote reconstruction changes no other source slot. Of its two
remaining erasures, the optional boundary completion above fills source 3;
source 78 in the ending `XAOKYYXRMYAQY?5X` remains unknown. The questionable
fixed closing labels are retained.

### Later conditional reading of the p214 closing label

The independent [late-key interpretation](../experiments/late_key_interpretation/README.md) applies the p217-derived Nov22–24 numeral hypothesis to the unchanged p214 B source. Its baseline `AOKYY` becomes `AOK11`, consistent with the 11th Army headquarters. The remaining reference stays damaged, and this optional map does not alter the earlier quoted body or its repair costs.

## p181 B — Repeated request for local armistice conditions

**Edition context:** Namur arrival, Cassel transport and armistice-information requests.

**Related source pages:** [p172 C1](172.md#source-p172-c1), [p172 C3](172.md#source-p172-c3), [p180 E](180.md#source-p180-e).

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-namur-arrival-cassel-transport-and-armistice-information-requests"></a>



**Source review and edition: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.**

These four surviving source bodies report an arrival at Namur, direct prompt transport arrangements to Cassel, and request the local armistice conditions again. The Namur telegram explicitly lacks its second part; its first and third parts are presented without bridging that gap. Literal office labels, an opaque transport field and source-length spellings remain visible.

<a id="source-p181-b"></a>
<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p181-b"></a>

### p181 B

**Source transcription — header:** `B) LP v NKJ (01.00 a.m., November 12th); 23.10 (12/11); RICHI-234`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> An OHL. OKM und AOK11. Erbitten nochmals Mitteilung der besonderen Waffenstillstandsbedingungen fuer hiesigen Kriegsschauplatz.

**Meaning:** The sender again asks OHL, OKM and the literal addressee AOK11 for the specific armistice conditions applying to the local theater of operations. The text is a request for information, not the conditions themselves.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
ANXOHLXXOKMXUNDAOK11XERBITTENNOCHMALSMITTEILU?GDERBESONDERENXWAFFENS2ILLSTAXDSBEDINGUNGENFQERHIESIGENKRIEGSSCHAUPLATZ
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 1 source-mask fill; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
ANXOHLXXOKMXUNDAOK11XERBITTENNOCHMALSMITTEILUNGDERBESONDERENXWAFFENSTILLSTANDSBEDINGUNGENFUERHIESIGENKRIEGSSCHAUPLATZ
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The printed source has one non-coordinate glyph O in OADDG. It occupies a source slot, is masked in the raw model, and is filled explicitly for MITTEILUNG.
- The lexical proposals WAFFENS2ILLSTAXDS to WAFFENSTILLSTANDS and FQER to FUER are priced observed-coordinate changes. The raw numeral-like 2 remains available in the exact raw layer.
- Both header times and the separate 12/11 line remain literal. The label AOK11 is not used to prove a historical unit identification.

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-evidence-and-credit"></a>

### Evidence and credit

Published period keys: George Lasry, Ingo Niebel, Nils Kopal and Arno Wacker (2016), and George Lasry (2017 key list). Earlier unreviewed repository candidates are retained separately. Source review and explicit editorial work: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.

The certificates replay every coordinate alteration, compare the independent column/domain reconstruction with the cipher implementation, and re-encrypt every complete edited output. For a partial output, an injective global completion of the square and residual source masks supplies an explicitly nonhistorical round-trip witness. Each readable passage preserves every nonseparator output label; literal protected fields are also checked without removing their internal separators. Source crops are bound to the original PDF by page, rectangle, scale, file digest and RGB-pixel digest.

Reproduce with `python experiments/namur_cassel_armistice_requests/verify.py --verify`. Add `--pdf /path/to/adfgvx-childs.pdf` to regenerate and compare the delivered source pixels.

A round-trip proves compatibility with a stated reading. Editorial spelling repairs remain proposals, and literal number labels are not automatically historical dates, quantities or reference numbers.

### p172 C1

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 1 TL RICHI-116`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> Major Kroeger. GHQU. Soeben mit RXABLASS Namur eingetroffen.

**Meaning:** The first surviving part names Major Kroeger and reports a recent arrival at Namur. The opening may address Kroeger, so the arriving person is not securely identified. GHQU and RXABLASS remain opaque labels. The surviving third part closes with Hpt. Mannstaedt, and the source explicitly marks part 2 as missing.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXIOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

**Edited output** — 1 observed-coordinate substitution and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
MAJORKROEGERXGHQUXSOEBENXMITXXRXABLASSXNAMURXEINGETROFFENX
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The native 116-slot first part is complete. The source explicitly prints “2 TL (Missing)” before the separately preserved third part; no second part is supplied or counted.
- IOEBEN to SOEBEN is an explicitly priced lexical proposal. GHQU and RXABLASS remain literal and unexpanded; ABLASS is not asserted to be a person's name. The opening could be an address, and no arriving subject is supplied.
- The printed time is 13.40 p.m. and is retained without conversion. No historical identity beyond the literal surname KROEGER is inferred.

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p172-c3"></a>

### p172 C3

**Source transcription — header:** `C) SY v ZM (13.40 p.m., November 10th); 1412 3 TLE; 3 TL RICHI-84`

**Readable German:** based on the unchanged raw output.

> Erbitten hierueber Bescheid. Hpt. Mannstaedt.

**Meaning:** The surviving third part asks for a response on the preceding matter and closes with the literal signature Hpt. Mannstaedt. The intervening second part is absent from the printed source.

<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

```text
ERBITTENXHIERUEBERXBESCHEIDXHPTXMANNSTAEDT
```

<a id="edition-cases-military-namur-cassel-armistice-requests-p180-e"></a>

### p180 E

**Source transcription — header:** `E) SY A v SY (10.09 p.m., November 12th); 10.45; RICHI-224`

**Readable German — repaired output:**

> Lt. Bauman. STATON sofort marschbereit 0 sein fuer M?TRANSPORT Cassel. Abtransport so schnell wie moeglich regeln. Kommandeur.

**Meaning:** The instruction addresses Lt. Bauman, calls for immediate readiness to move, and directs transport to Cassel to be arranged as quickly as possible. The spelling STATON and the literal fields 0 and M? TRANSPORT remain unresolved; the specific transport type is not identified.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output** — every native source slot in printed order, under the stated published key.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBERECT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELSWIEMOEGLICHRE?ELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

**Edited output** — 3 observed-coordinate substitutions and 0 source-mask fills; no coordinate inserted, deleted or moved.

```text
LTXBAUMANXSTATONSOFORTXMARSCHBEREIT0SEINFUERXM?TRANSPORTXCASSELXABTRANSPORTSOSCHNELLWIEMOEGLICHREGELNXKOMMANDEUR
```

</details>

**Unresolved details and editorial limits:**

- The source contains 224 slots, including all final groups; no coordinate is inserted, removed or moved.
- STATON is retained without inserting the absent I of STATION. BAUMAN remains the literal surname with one terminal N.
- MARSCHBERECT0 to MARSCHBEREIT0, SCHNELS to SCHNELL and RE?ELN to REGELN are separately priced lexical changes. The literal 0 is not silently changed into a separator.
- The Nov13–15b published key is used because it yields the demonstrated reading; the printed 12 November date is retained as a different evidence layer.
- The unknown position in M?TRANSPORT comes from an unresolved square cell and remains globally coupled. Its label is not chosen from historical expectations.

</details>
